title: The meter refuses in two different wire shapes: DL-19 puts its codes in error.code (delegation-refusal), but DL-21 and verifyMeterToken answer a grant-check `denied` document, and no rule maps one to the other
evidence: delegation.md:226-228 says `a callee, the hub and the meter refuse with these codes only, kebab-case, in error.code ... (delegation-refusal.schema.json)`. delegation.md:285-288 says the meter `maps any verifier refusal to principal-unproven (verifyMeterToken) ... and answers a grant-check document`. src/delegation.ts:356 returns `{ ok: false, denial: GrantCheckDenied }`, where `code` is top-level and `window` is top-level (grant-check.schema.json), but delegation-refusal puts window/level under error.data. Neither spec says whether a meter denial is an MCP isError result carrying a delegation-refusal or a successful result carrying grant-check `denied`, or how the callee turns a `denied` (level, window) into its own `limit-reached` refusal (DL-19 table: `limit-reached` refused by `meter, callee`).
status_measured: measured by reading spec, schema and code at 8e49fbd
proposed_fix: State in DL-19 that the meter's form is the grant-check document (a `denied` is a normal result, not isError), and add a DL-21 step: a callee refusing its caller after a `denied` copies `code` to error.code and `window`/`level` to error.data. Add a test converting grant-check-denied.json into a valid delegation-refusal.

title: A per-call refusal (L3, perCallMaxUsd) cannot be expressed: `limit-reached` requires a `window`, and no window means `call`
source: docs/specification/spend-policy.md:23, :50; schemas/grant-check.schema.json (window enum, allOf limit-reached); schemas/delegation-refusal.schema.json (data.window enum, allOf limit-reached)
evidence: spend-policy.md:23 defines L3 call (`perCallMaxUsd`). Both schemas require `window` with `limit-reached`, and the enum is exactly [total, task, project, day, week, month] (grant-check.schema.json `window`; delegation-refusal.schema.json `data.window`). A meter that refuses an amount above perCallMaxUsd must either name a window that was not reached or produce an invalid document.
proposed_fix: Add a `call` value to the refusal window enums (both schemas and the grant's spend vocabulary note), or make window optional when level is L3. Add a positive fixture for a per-call denial.

title: The `task` window (DEC-0038) cannot be enforced: neither the token nor the grant-check request names a task
evidence: spend-policy.md:47 says `task: one task`. grant-check-request.schema.json allows only amountUsd, tokenJti, grantRef and purpose (additionalProperties false). delegation-token.schema.json has no task claim (additionalProperties false). The meter has nothing to group a task's spend by, so the task window of delegation-mint-ok.json's grant (`{window: task, limitUsd: 2}`) cannot be enforced as written.
proposed_fix: Add an optional task id: a `task` claim minted from the caller's run, or a `task` field in grant-check-request. Say which side the meter trusts, and add a fixture.

title: Who holds the grant the meter reserves against is unspecified: the hub decides grants and a token carries only opaque references, yet spend policy says every limit lives in one registry
evidence: delegation.md:38: the issuer `decides grants with the operator`. delegation.md:64: a grant reference is formed by the issuer, and `a callee and a usage reader treat it as opaque`. spend-policy.md:11: `Every limit is a grant in one registry`. delegation.md:42: the meter `reserves spend against the grant's windows`. No section says how the meter gets the windows behind `urn:grant:...#3`: a registry copy, a hub projection or a lookup. The handoff's Open list (docs/handoffs/2026-10-11-delegation-and-fabric-button.md:37-39) places `access_grants` in Fabric and grant-check in Observatory.
needs: check against DEC-0041 PR (readProjectedGrant); decision: which store is the grant's record and how the meter reads it — Fabric (ADR-0144 owner) with Project Observatory
proposed_fix: Specify the projection: what the hub publishes per grant (ref, windows, perCallMaxUsd, state, expiry), how the meter reads it, and that a missing projection is `unknown-state`.

title: The token's `grant` claim is an array, but FAC-SEM-050 accepts extra grant references the token was not minted under, and the meter lets the callee pick one
source: src/delegation-rules.ts:81-82; schemas/delegation-token.schema.json `grant` (maxItems 8); schemas/grant-check-request.schema.json `grantRef`; schemas/service-usage.schema.json byGrant[].grantRef; docs/specification/delegation.md:64, :93-95
evidence: DL-4 (delegation.md:93-95): a token is minted under one delegation grant and names it. FAC-SEM-050 only checks `strings(token.grant).includes(ref)` (delegation-rules.ts:82). Probe: delegation-mint-ok.json with token.grant = [its ref, 'urn:grant:project-a:unlimited-other#3'] gives `extra grant ref -> []` (npx tsx probe2.mts). grant-check-request.grantRef (`Which of the token's grants, when it names several`) has no rule that it is one of the token's grants, so a callee can choose which grant the meter reserves against.
status_measured: measured: probe output, FAC-SEM-050 returns no finding
needs: check against DEC-0041 PR; decision: whether `grant` is exactly one reference (maxItems 1), or what several grants mean for minting and metering — contract maintainer with the Fabric ADR-0144 owner
proposed_fix: Either make `grant` one reference, or have FAC-SEM-050 refuse a reference that is not the grant (or, for the meter token, the parent's). Require grant-check-request.grantRef to be one of the token's grants, so the meter refuses `no-grant` otherwise. Add the probe as a semantic fixture.

title: A callee at the maximum chain depth can never be metered: its onward token for the meter would have five actors
evidence: DL-21 adds the callee as the outermost actor of the meter token. DL-6 and the verifier cap the chain at four. Probe (npx tsx probe.mts): a callee token with 4 actors gives `ok`; its meter token gives `principal-unproven: the meter's token was refused: chain-too-deep (depth-5)`. The schema cannot even hold it (actor4 has no `act`). So a fourth-hop callee can be called but cannot pass a grant check before spending.
needs: check against DEC-0041 PR; decision: exempt the meter hop from DL-6, or cap spending callees at depth 3 — Fabric ADR-0144 owner with the contract maintainer
proposed_fix: Record the choice in DL-6/DL-21, align the schema (actor5 for meter tokens only, or a depth note), and test the depth-4 case.

title: verifyDelegation accepts claims that DL-13 step 5 refuses, and refuses in a different order than the table, so a port that follows the table will answer different codes
evidence: DL-13 row 5: `the claims have the DL-2 types` -> unauthenticated, checked before rows 7-8. delegationShape only checks strings/ints/effect/grant, and checks act for isObject only. Probe (npx tsx probe.mts): `act.sub 'Not An Agent Id!', session:42, jti:'x', project:7, spend:'lots'` gives `ok` (and returns caller 'Not An Agent Id!'); scope 'writer.write  writer.check' (two spaces, against the schema pattern) gives `ok`; a malformed chain with a wrong aud gives `wrong-audience/audience-mismatch`, and when expired `token-expired/expired`, instead of `unauthenticated`. delegation.md:168: `A verifier in another language follows the same table`.
proposed_fix: In delegationShape, check the DL-2 types: act chain members (sub against AGENT_ID, session pattern), jti pattern, scope pattern, project and spend shape when present. Move the malformed-chain check before the lifetime and audience checks. Add a test row for each.

title: Twelve FAC-SEM-050 sub-checks can be deleted with every test still passing
evidence: Mutation probes on a copy (rsync without .git; each line replaced by `if (false)` or similar; `npx vitest run test/`). Each of these left `698 passed (698)`: M3 meter token without parent (:98), M4 session actor (:116), M5 external sub (:111), M6 onward keeps project (:124), M7 onward chain equals the parent's (:126), M8 a limited parent mints a limited child (:135), M9 onward keeps iss (:123), M10 token outlives grant (:86), M11 sub is the grant's issuer (:118), M12 meter token names only the parent's grants (:97), M32 meter token effect exactly [none] (:96, hidden by the parent-ceiling finding in delegation-mint-meter-wide.json), M36 malformed agent/session principal (:113). By contrast M33/M34/M35 failed 1 test each.
proposed_fix: Add one semantic fixture per sub-check (session-mismatch, external-sub, sub-not-issuer, outlives-grant, onward-project, onward-chain, onward-iss, limited-parent-unlimited-child, meter-without-parent, meter-foreign-grant, meter-effect with a parent whose ceiling admits it, bad-principal). Assert one path each, as delegation-seams.test.ts §3 does.

title: Security MUSTs of the verifier and approval checker have no failing test: crit/x5u/x5c headers, a published private key, the approval's issuer and future iat, the typ gate in readDelegationToken, and the meter's issuer
evidence: Mutation probes with `npx vitest run test/`, all leaving `698 passed (698)`: M24 header refusal list reduced to [jku, jwk] (DL-1 refuses crit, x5u, x5c); M23 `jwk.d !== undefined` removed (a private member is accepted as a key); M14 approval wrong-issuer removed; M15 approval issued-in-future removed (DL-18 `the lifetime, the 60 s leeway`); M16 `parsed.header.typ === DELEGATION_TYP` removed (DL-16: only a bearer whose typ is fabric-delegation+jwt is a delegation token; every other JWT bearer would now be taken from the product's own auth); M18 issuer no longer passed through verifyMeterToken; M25 signature length check removed.
proposed_fix: Add cases to the test/delegation.test.ts unauthenticated table: header-crit, header-x5u, header-x5c, and a JWK carrying `d` (unusable-key). In the approval-invalid table: wrong-issuer and issued-in-future. Assert readDelegationToken returns undefined for an approval-typ JWT bearer. Assert verifyMeterToken refuses a wrong iss when the issuer is given.

source: docs/specification/spend-policy.md:96-97; docs/specification/delegation.md:263-265 (DL-20); schemas/grant-check.schema.json allOf/then/properties/level; schemas/governance.schema.json:62 dependentRequired

title: The operator-session lifetime tightens an existing service MUST while DEC-0039 calls itself additive; 'descriptor token rotates' is undefined, and the never-lengthen clamp on the 7-day bound is untested
source: docs/specification/service.md:249-255; docs/DECISIONS.md DEC-0039 Compatibility (`Additive under DEC-0016`); docs/DECISIONS.md:155-165 (DEC-0016: `nothing required changes`); docs/handoffs/2026-10-11-delegation-and-fabric-button.md:47-48; src/operator-session.ts:18, :27
evidence: service.md:252-253: a service `MUST NOT lengthen` 12 h idle / 7 days max. Handoff:47: `their operator session cookie lives 30 days`, so every kit-built service is nonconformant from the merge, against DEC-0016's `nothing required changes` and DEC-0039's `Additive`. service.md:251 `when the descriptor token rotates` is the only mention of rotation in service.md (no rotation procedure; `tokenRevision` exists only in src/operator-session.ts:18). Mutation M1 (`const max = policy.maxSeconds ?? ...`, removing the clamp) leaves 698/698 pass: test/delegation.test.ts:288 cannot tell, because the idle bound dominates.
status_measured: measured: mutation survived (698/698 pass) and read

title: verifyMeterToken's `readOnly: true` does nothing: the meter accepts an onward token whose ceiling is [send, charge]
evidence: verifyMeterToken passes effect 'none', and the read-only door fires only when `effect !== 'none'` (delegation.ts:310), so it never fires. Probe: meter token with effect ['send','charge'] gives `ok`. Mutation M17 (readOnly false) leaves 698/698 pass. DL-21 step 3 and the conformance row say the meter verifies `effect none`, but only the issuer rule (FAC-SEM-050) checks it.
status_measured: measured: probe output and mutation survived
proposed_fix: In verifyMeterToken, refuse unless claims.effect is exactly ['none'] (and scope is exactly the capability), or reword DL-21/conformance to say the meter relies on the issuer for these. Test it.

title: The issuer check is optional in the kit verifier, although DL-13 row 5 requires it and DL-16 makes the issuer mandatory
evidence: DL-13 row 5: `iss is the issuer the callee trusts`. DL-16: `auth.delegation: {issuer, jwks}` (issuer required in the schema). verifyDelegation's `issuer?` skips the check when omitted. Probe: iss 'urn:fabric:estate:someone-else' without the option gives `ok`. The conformance reader row (conformance.md:60) does not list the issuer.
proposed_fix: Make `issuer` required in VerifyDelegationOptions/VerifyApprovalOptions/VerifyMeterOptions, or document that omitting it trusts any iss under the estate key, and add the issuer to the conformance row.

The schema and verifier accept the value.

title: Two different 'canonical JSON' forms sign or hash estate documents (RFC 8785 jcs for approvals; the settings-backup canonicalJson for device policies) and nothing tells them apart
source: src/delegation.ts:395-420; src/settings-backup.ts:20-37; docs/specification/service.md:430-435; docs/specification/devices.md:151-156; docs/specification/delegation.md:203; CONTEXT.md:93
evidence: Probe (npx tsx canon.mts) on {b:1, a:['x',true], '😀':1, '｡':2}: jcs gives `{"a":["x",true],"b":1,"😀":1,"｡":2}`, while canonicalJson gives `{"a": ["x", true], "b": 1, "｡": 2, "😀": 1}`. These differ in separators and in key order (UTF-16 against code point), and canonicalJson also refuses fractions. devices.md:156 signs a policy over `canonical JSON`; delegation.md:203 digests an action over `RFC 8785 canonical JSON (JCS)`. No glossary entry or cross-reference separates them, and a kit port can reuse the wrong one.
proposed_fix: Add CONTEXT.md entries for `canonical JSON (settings form)` and `JCS (RFC 8785)`, a sentence in DL-17 saying the action digest is not service.md's canonicalJson, and a test asserting that the two differ on the probe value.

title: External citations missing from the source ledger or without retrieval: WCAG 2.2 and RFC 2119 have no row, seven RFC rows were 'not re-fetched', and Fabric ADR-0144 is linked at an unmerged branch
source: docs/specification/fabric-button.md:40; docs/specification/delegation.md:3, :20; docs/evidence/sources.md:30-33, :37-39; docs/DECISIONS.md DEC-0039 Status/Amends lines

RFC 2119 is cited in 8 specification files, with no row. sources.md:30-33 and :37-39 (RFC 7519, 7515, 7517, 8037, 6750, 7662, 3986) say `from the RFC text; not re-fetched in this run, 2026-10-11`, which is no retrieval date. delegation.md:3 and DEC-0039 link `fabric/blob/agent/release-040-wave1/docs/adr/0144-...` and the adoption plan on the same branch: a moving branch, not a commit.

title: The credential-name rule refuses ordinary parameter names (country_code, sort_key, pass), which breaks FL-2's 'unknown parameters are ignored'
evidence: Probe: `fabric://chat?service=example-agent&country_code=PL`, `&sort_key=name` and `&pass=1` each give `the parameter ... could carry a credential; a link never does`. FL-4 refuses a name that `can only carry a credential`, but SECRET_NAME treats any `code`, `key`, `pass`, `auth` or `sig` word segment as a credential. A newer page adding such a parameter is refused whole by an older Fabric, against FL-2.
proposed_fix: Narrow SECRET_NAME to whole credential names and compound forms (token, *_token, secret, password, api_key, private_key, login_code, auth_code, session_id, cookie, jwt), keep the value-shape check, and add `country_code`/`sort_key` as accepted cases in test/fabric-button.test.ts.

title: FB-6's fabric_button cookie leaves out ED-8's 'page's own storage partition' and gives no lifetime, so a stale owner=host can hide the button where no host draws one
evidence: ED-8 (embedded-dashboard.md:75-76): set `in the page's own storage partition on the service origin`. FB-6 (fabric-button.md:68-70) copies only `path /, SameSite=Strict, not HttpOnly, Secure on https` and says nothing about partition or expiry. A host writing `owner=host` into a shared cookie jar makes the page hide its button in a plain browser tab, where FB-1 then leaves zero buttons.
proposed_fix: In FB-6, require the page's own storage partition (as ED-8 does) and a session cookie (no Max-Age/Expires), or require the page to show its button when the host is not present.

title: DL-13 row 3 calls an unusable published key the issuer's fault (issuer-unavailable), but a key with use≠sig or alg≠EdDSA is answered unauthenticated
source: docs/specification/delegation.md:151; src/delegation.ts:214, :235; test/delegation-seams.test.ts:188-189; schemas/delegation-jwks.schema.json (use const sig, alg const EdDSA)
evidence: delegation.md:151: `a published key that cannot be used, or a kid published twice, is the issuer's fault | unauthenticated; issuer-unavailable`. Code: key-not-for-signing becomes unauthenticated (delegation.ts:235 marks only unusable-key/duplicate-kid as the issuer's). The test expects `unauthenticated/key-not-for-signing`. Yet such a key makes the published set invalid against delegation-jwks.schema.json, which is the issuer's fault.
proposed_fix: Pick one answer and state it in row 3 explicitly (`use`/`alg` mismatch -> issuer-unavailable is consistent with the schema), then align the code and test/delegation-seams.test.ts §11.

title: FAC-SEM-050 does not check that a token's `spend` matches its grant (DL-4 'carries what remains'), nor that an onward token's perCallMaxUsd stays within its parent's
evidence: delegation-rules.ts:91 only checks `tokenSpend?.mode !== 'limited'`: remaining windows the grant lacks, or remainingUsd above the grant's limitUsd, pass. Probe: onward token perCallMaxUsd 999 under a parent with perCallMaxUsd 1 gives `perCallMax above parent -> []`. `spend` informs and never authorizes (delegation.md:73-74), so the impact is a misleading claim, not overspend.
proposed_fix: Under a limited grant, require each remaining window to be one of the grant's limits and at most its limitUsd, and perCallMaxUsd at most the grant's (onward: at most the parent's). Add fixtures.
